I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life — more than sixty years now. My body is old, my back hurts in the cold, and my son comes back only during the busiest weeks. But I know this land. I know what it needs.

Here in Quzhou we do wheat in winter and maize in summer. That is what everyone does. That is what my father did. I will not change that. I have about 5 mu of land I can still manage. I will plant all of it — wheat first, then maize on the same ground after harvest. I cannot afford to let it sit idle.

For seeds, I go to the village supply cooperative. They sell the improved wheat variety — Jimai 22 I think, or whatever the county extension people brought this year. For maize, I buy hybrid seed, Xianyu 335 maybe, because the yield is better and everyone does it now. Traditional seed I haven't used in thirty years.

Fertilizer: I apply compound fertilizer before seeding, then urea top-dressing for the wheat in spring. I learned these amounts from my neighbors decades ago. I don't measure precisely — I go by feel and habit. Probably more than the books say, but it is what I know.

Irrigation: the well is shared. Wheat needs water in winter jointing and again before heading — I will water three times. Maize I water once or twice depending on the rains. The pump is heavy and tiring, but my neighbor's son sometimes helps.

Pesticide: I spray wheat for aphids and rust in spring, one or two times. Maize I watch for armyworm — one spray usually.

Tillage: I rent the rotary tiller from the village machine station before wheat planting. For maize after wheat harvest, I plant straight into the stubble — no-tillage, saves my back and saves money.

I expect maybe 400 jin per mu for wheat, 500 jin for maize. Not the best yields in the village but enough for us to eat and a little to sell.
